newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares rise in late rally, prospects unclear.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares rise in late rally, prospects unclear.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Friday boosted by recommendations to buy Tele Danmark and Den Danske Bank paper, with dealers unsure about next week's prospects.

"Goldman Sachs are recommending buying Tele Danmark and there's another recommendation circulating advising investors to drop Unibank shares in favour of Den Danske Bank. This helped the index close higher after a late rally," one dealer said.
He said the top-20 KFX index would keep between the 119-120.50 range on Monday after closing for the weekend 0.24 point up at 119.51 in overall 1.397 billion crown turnover.
The KFX September future fell 0.20 point to 119.75 with 209 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
In the event, Den Danske Bank put on five crowns to finish at 408, while rival Unibank shod four to end at 253.

Tele Danmark was the day's busiest share with 362,000 shares traded to close seven crowns higher at 282, while Sophus Berendsen lost seven crowns to 685 after a 1996 interim result which failed to impress the market.
Shipper Lauritzen plunged 100 crowns to close at 500 after delivering a disastrous 1996 half-year result with more losses and a shipyard closure ahead.
